0.0.n: A playful greeting borrowed from Italian, with a stretched vowel.

0.2.n: This is part of the name みぽち, not a form of 見る.

0.3.n: The split is misleading: ち finishes the name みぽち, and だ is the casual form of です.

0.4.n: よ adds a friendly announcement tone; the long vowel makes it playful.

1.0.n: Here はい introduces the next announcement rather than answering a question.

1.2.n: やってまいりました is a polite, humble version of やってきました, giving the introduction a presenter-like tone.

1.4.n: This begins the channel name みぽちゅーぶ; it is not a form of 見る.

1.5.n: This character belongs to the channel name みぽちゅーぶ and has no separate meaning here.

1.6.n: This finishes the channel name; ちゅーぶ playfully echoes the English word tube.

2.0.n: An adjective alone can be a complete exclamation in Japanese.

2.2.n: This time word sets the scene without needing a particle.

2.3.n: A very casual intensifier used before the adjective 寒い.

2.4.n: The adjective keeps its plain form before the explanatory んだ.

2.5.n: ん is shortened の, adding an explanatory or emphatic tone before だ.

2.6.n: だ completes the casual explanatory ending んだ; it does not attach directly to 寒い.

2.7.n: けど contrasts the cold weather with her plan to go out anyway.

2.9.n: Repeated here to introduce today's filming plan.

2.10.n: も attaches to 今日, suggesting she is doing this today as on other days.

2.11.n: This points to what she is about to do next.

2.12.n: A place name for a district in Tokyo, here specifying the filming location.

2.13.n: ロケ is shortened ロケーション and refers to filming outside a studio.

2.14.n: に marks the purpose of going: a location shoot.

2.15.n: 行く changes to 行きたい with たい, which expresses wanting to do something.

2.16.n: と marks 行きたい as the thought expressed by 思います.

2.17.n: The polite form of 思う; with たいと, it gently announces her intention.

3.0.n: At the start of speech, で casually connects this announcement to what came before.

3.2.n: This time word identifies when she will ask the questions.

3.3.n: も presents today's interviewing as something she has done on other occasions.

3.4.n: ね adds a friendly, conversational tone and draws the listener in.

3.6.n: 聞く in its て-form plus いく presents the questioning as an activity unfolding from now.

3.7.n: の turns 聞いていく into a noun-like phrase: what she will be asking.

3.8.n: が marks what she will ask about, though she restarts the sentence afterward.

3.9.n: 黒 combines with 歴史 in 黒歴史, meaning an embarrassing past rather than a literal color.

3.10.n: Here it completes 黒歴史, a common expression for past experiences someone would rather hide.

3.11.n: と links the two interview topics: embarrassing pasts and biggest blunders.

3.12.n: 今 combines with まで to establish the time span up to the present.

3.13.n: まで marks the endpoint in 今まで, covering someone's life up to now.

3.14.n: で sets the range for 一番: everything that has happened so far.

3.15.n: 一番 makes the following mistake the biggest one within the stated time span.

3.16.n: やらかしちゃった is casual やらかしてしまった, describing a completed blunder, often with regret.

3.17.n: こと turns the preceding description into the event or incident she wants to hear about.

3.18.n: を marks the interview topics as what she wants to ask about.

3.19.n: 聞いていく becomes 聞いていきたい with たい, expressing her desire to proceed with the interviews.

3.20.n: と introduces the preceding wish as the content of 思います.

3.21.n: The polite ending たいと思います presents what she plans to do, rather than uncertainty.

4.0.n: Drop the final い of 寒い and add すぎる to express excess.

4.1.n: けど contrasts the extreme cold with her determination to carry on.

4.3.n: これ refers to the drink she is indicating or holding.

4.4.n: を marks これ as what she will drink.

4.5.n: The て-form of 飲む connects drinking with the following action, 頑張る.

4.6.n: The plain form expresses her resolve to keep going despite the cold.

4.8.n: An English expression written in katakana, used as an energetic send-off.

0.tip: The name is みぽち; the subtitle splits it incorrectly across word buttons.

1.lit: All right, here we have come, Mipotube!
1.tip: やってまいりました gives this playful channel introduction a polite presenter-style flourish.

2.lit: Cold! Today really cold, but today too, from now, for Shibuya filming, I think I want to go.
2.tip: たいと思います often announces a plan politely rather than expressing an uncertain wish.

3.lit: And today too, what we'll ask: embarrassing pasts and biggest mess-ups so far—I think I want to ask.
3.tip: This spoken sentence restarts midway; 黒歴史 and the biggest blunder are the two interview topics.

4.lit: Too cold, but I'll drink this and do my best. Let's go!
4.tip: すぎる means too much; 寒い loses its final い to become 寒すぎる.
